title: Import a session from a WhatsApp group member-list screenshot
risk: Children end up enrolled under the wrong names, or the AI makes up children, so families are billed and messaged wrongly.
preconditions: You are signed in as the Boss on a computer.

You have a test school to import into, with an obvious name such as “AUDIT TEST – delete me”. Agree with the owner beforehand how the test families will be removed, because every child on a session is invoiced automatically on the 1st.

You have a screenshot of a WhatsApp group’s participant list (Group info → Participants) with 4–6 members. Some should be saved by name and some should show only as a phone number. The owner’s own entry (“You”) should also be visible. Use test or colleague numbers, not real parents.
steps: Go to Schools and press “Import a roster”.
Under School, choose “+ New school” and type the test school name. Under Session, choose “+ New session”, type “Audit WhatsApp” and leave the monthly fee at 100. Press “Next”.

Press “Add screenshots or a CSV” and choose the WhatsApp screenshot. Check that its file name appears in the list, then press “Read roster”. Note how long it takes (the screen says screenshots take about half a minute).
On the review screen, read the summary line (“N children found. N need a fix before they can be added.”) and compare every row with the screenshot.
Check that the owner’s own entry (“You” or admin) does not appear as a row.
For each row, type the child’s first and last name, then click out of the field.
Press “Import N children”.
expected: There is one row per parent in the screenshot. Each parent’s name (where shown) and phone number are copied exactly, digit for digit.
The child first name is blank on every row. Each row is outlined in amber with “Child's first name is missing”, which shows the AI does not make up children’s names.
Where the AI filled in the child’s last name from the parent’s surname, that field is highlighted in amber.
Members shown only as a number have a blank parent name. Once the child’s names are filled in, those rows are still held back with “Parent's name is missing” until you type a parent name.
After all required names are filled in, each row shows a green “Ready” and the number on the Import button goes up to match.
The done screen says “N children added to AUDIT TEST… · Audit WhatsApp.” and “N new families”.
If a red message says “Reading screenshots isn't switched on yet…” instead, the AI reader is not turned on in the live app. Record this as a blocking exception for ROS-01 and ROS-02.
evidence: The original screenshot, the review screen before and after filling in child names (with the amber rows visible), and the done screen.

Find the blurry or cut-off phone number and check that its box is highlighted in amber.
Correct that phone number and click out of the field. Check that the amber highlight on that field goes away.
Compare every other row with the original spreadsheet, field by field.
Press “Back”, remove the screenshots with the X, add only the non-roster photo and press “Read roster”.

expected: Rows from both screenshots appear in one list. Where the screenshots overlap, no row is repeated. If one is, note it; it can be removed with the bin icon.

11 screenshots give “Up to 10 screenshots at a time, please.”
evidence: Both original screenshots, the review screen showing the amber field(s) and the notes box, and the two error messages.

title: The first-login tour starts once, can be skipped, can be replayed from the menu, and doesn’t restart on another device

risk: Families are charged the wrong amount, or the card fee is not what the payment page showed, which leads to disputes and refunds and damages trust.
preconditions: Stripe is in Test mode (Settings → Payments shows Test, and the Stripe dashboard has 'Test mode' / sandbox switched on).
Settings → Payments: 'Enable Stripe' is on and 'Card Fee (%)' is set to a known value (default 3). Write the value down.
A test family (Parent A) with one child actively enrolled, an invoice for the current month showing 'pending' or 'overdue' on Payments → Invoices, a phone number, and an email address you can read.
Parent A's autopay is off.
steps: As Boss, go to Payments → Invoices. Find Parent A's invoice and write down the Amount. Click the link icon in the 'Pay link' column ('Copy this family's payment page link').
Open the link on your phone.
Check the top of the page: 'Hi <first name>', 'Payments for <child first name>.', and under 'To pay' a total equal to the invoice amount.

Under 'Pay automatically', read the two buttons. 'Bank account' should say 'No fee'. 'Card' should say '<your %>% card fee'. Read the small print: 'Your current balance of $X will be paid within a day.'
Tap 'Card'. On the Stripe page, enter card 4242 4242 4242 4242, any future expiry, any CVC and any ZIP, then save.
When you are sent back, check the page.
Wait for the next daily run (about 1 pm Central; noon after the clocks change in November), or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Reopen the payment page. Then, as Boss, check Payments → Invoices and Payments → Payment History.
In the Stripe dashboard (Test mode), open Payments, find the newest payment and open it.
Check the email inbox for Parent A.
expected: Before choosing, the page shows the card fee percentage and the bank 'No fee' label.
After returning from Stripe: a green box 'You're all set.' and 'Autopay is on — Paid from Visa ••••4242 on each due date, plus a <x>% card fee.'
The 'Prefer Zelle?' section is no longer shown.
After the daily run, the invoice status is 'paid' and the payment page says 'You're all paid up'.

Payment History has one new row: Method 'stripe', Amount equal to the invoice balance (the fee is NOT in this column), Reference 'Visa ••••4242'. Opening the row's edit (pencil) shows Notes 'Autopay (card fee $F)'.
The Stripe charge amount equals balance + fee, where fee = balance × fee% rounded to the nearest cent. The description reads '<Month> — <child first name>'.
Parent A gets one email, 'Receipt: $<total> received — <business name>', listing the child line, 'Card processing fee $F' and a 'Total' equal to the Stripe amount.
evidence: Phone screenshots of the fee labels before choosing and of 'Autopay is on'. Screenshot of the Stripe payment detail showing the amount. Screenshots of the Payment History row and its Notes. The receipt email. A short calculation note: balance × % = fee.

title: Set up bank autopay with Test Institution and confirm no fee is charged
risk: Bank-paying families are charged a card fee, or a bank debit is never collected or booked.
preconditions: Stripe is in Test mode.
Test family Parent B with one open invoice and autopay off; Parent B's email is readable.
steps: Copy Parent B's pay link from Payments → Invoices and open it on your phone.
Tap 'Bank account' ('No fee').
In Stripe's bank picker, choose 'Test Institution', then pick the successful test account and finish.
Check the page you return to.
Wait for the next daily run (about 1 pm Central), or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Immediately after the run, reload Parent B's payment page and look at Payments → Invoices.
In the Stripe dashboard (Test mode), look at the payment for Parent B. Test-mode bank debits can settle within minutes, so check soon.
After Stripe shows the payment 'Succeeded', recheck Payments → Invoices, Payment History and Parent B's email.
expected: After setup: 'Autopay is on — Paid from <Bank name> ••••<last4> on each due date. You'll never need to send anything.' No card-fee wording.
While the debit is in flight, the invoice shows 'processing' and the payment page lists the line with 'Bank payment on its way'. It is not under 'To pay'.
The Stripe amount equals the invoice balance exactly, with no fee added.
Once settled: the invoice is 'paid', Payment History has one 'stripe' row whose Amount equals the balance, and the Notes say 'Autopay' with no fee.
One receipt email with no 'Card processing fee' line.
evidence: Phone screenshots of the 'Bank payment on its way' state and of 'Autopay is on'. The Stripe payment timeline showing Processing then Succeeded. The Payment History row. The receipt email.

title: Check that siblings are charged once per family, in one charge
risk: A parent with two children sees two charges and gets two failure messages, or is double-charged.
preconditions: Stripe is in Test mode.
Test Parent C is linked to two children (e.g. Ava and Ben), each with an open invoice for this month.
Card Fee (%) is known.
steps: Open Parent C's pay link. Confirm 'Payments for Ava and Ben.' and that the 'To pay' total equals both invoices added together.
Tap 'Card' and save 4242 4242 4242 4242.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
In Stripe (Test mode), go to Payments and filter or search for Parent C's customer.
Check Payments → Payment History, Payments → Invoices and Parent C's email.
expected: Stripe shows exactly ONE payment for Parent C. Its description is '<Month> — Ava and Ben'.
Stripe amount = (Ava balance + Ava fee) + (Ben balance + Ben fee). The fee is worked out per invoice and rounded to the cent, so it can differ by 1 cent from the total × %. Record both figures.
Payment History shows TWO rows, one per child, each for that child's balance, both with the same Reference (card label).
Both invoices are 'paid'.
Exactly ONE receipt email lists both children, the card fee and a Total equal to the Stripe amount.
evidence: Stripe customer page showing a single payment. Payment History filtered to the two children. The receipt email. Your reconciliation arithmetic.

title: Check that an earlier unpaid month is rolled into the same charge, and a partial payment is respected
risk: A family is charged for a month already partly paid, or an older debt is never collected.
preconditions: Stripe is in Test mode.
Test Parent D has an unpaid invoice from LAST month (status 'overdue') and an invoice for THIS month.
On Payments → Invoices, use 'Record Payment' on last month's invoice row to record a partial cash payment (e.g. $20) against last month's invoice. Note the remaining balance.
Parent D's autopay is off.
steps: Open Parent D's pay link. Check that both months are listed under 'To pay'. Last month should show 'Was due <date>' in red, and the total should equal (last month remaining + this month).
Set up card autopay with 4242 4242 4242 4242.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Check Stripe, Payment History, Invoices and the receipt.
expected: One Stripe charge. Its description names both months (e.g. 'September and October — <child>').
The charge covers the REMAINING balance of last month (not the full original amount) plus this month, plus the card fee on each.
Payment History has two new 'stripe' rows (one per invoice) alongside the earlier $20 cash row.
Both invoices are 'paid'. One receipt email.
evidence: Pay page screenshot before setup. The Stripe charge. Payment History showing the cash row and the two stripe rows. Arithmetic.

title: Check that a bank debit in 'processing' gets no overdue reminder
risk: A family whose money is already on its way receives a payment-chasing WhatsApp and email, which looks unprofessional and causes complaints.
preconditions: Settings: payment reminders are enabled. Note 'payment reminder days after due' (default 3).
Test Parent E has an invoice that is overdue by MORE than that many days and has not been reminded yet (ask Mutaaf to prepare one if needed).
Parent E has a phone number and an email.
steps: Before the run, open Messaging → Outbox and note whether anything is waiting for Parent E.
Open Parent E's pay link and set up 'Bank account' with Test Institution (success account).
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Straight afterwards, check Payments → Invoices for Parent E's invoice status.
Check Messaging → Outbox and Parent E's email inbox for a payment reminder.
After Stripe shows the debit settled, check again.
expected: The invoice moves to 'processing' (or straight to 'paid' if test mode settled instantly), never to 'overdue' in that run.
No payment reminder appears in the Outbox, and no reminder email arrives for Parent E.
Once settled, the invoice is 'paid' and only a receipt email arrives.
evidence: Invoices list screenshot showing 'processing'. Outbox screenshot with no reminder for Parent E. The inbox showing only a receipt.

title: Check that a declined card means one message, one email, the invoice owed again, and no daily retry
risk: Failures go unnoticed, the parent is spammed, or the same declined card is retried daily and collects decline fees.
preconditions: Stripe is in Test mode.
Test Parent F has one or two children with open invoices, a phone and an email, and autopay is off.
Messaging → Outbox is clear of Parent F messages.
steps: Open Parent F's pay link and tap 'Card'. Enter 4000 0000 0000 0341. Saving it should succeed.
Confirm the page says 'Autopay is on' with 'Visa ••••0341'.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Check Payments → Invoices, Messaging → Outbox, and Parent F's email.
Reload Parent F's payment page.
Wait for the FOLLOWING day's run (or ask Mutaaf to trigger it again). Check Stripe, the Outbox and email again.
expected: Stripe shows one failed payment attempt (declined).
The invoice goes back to 'pending' or 'overdue' (owed), not 'paid' or 'processing'. No Payment History row is added.

Exactly ONE WhatsApp message for the family (even with two children) is in the Outbox: 'Hi <name>, the automatic payment of $<owed> for <children>'s <program> didn't go through (your card was declined…). You can update your payment details or pay another way here: <link>'. The $ amount is the balance owed (no card fee); note this.
Exactly ONE email: 'Your automatic payment didn't go through — <business name>'.

The payment page lists the invoice under 'To pay' again and, under 'Autopay is on', shows a red notice 'Your last automatic payment didn't go through' with the bank's reason, plus buttons to use a different card or switch to bank. The Zelle option reappears.
On the next day's run: NO new Stripe attempt, no second WhatsApp, no second email.
evidence: The Stripe failed payment. The Outbox message text. The failure email. Invoices status. A screenshot from the following day showing no new attempt in Stripe.

title: Check that a declined family is retried after saving a new card
risk: A family who fixes their card is never charged, and the debt quietly sits unpaid.
preconditions: PAY-06 completed: Parent F's invoice is owed after a decline and was not retried.
steps: Open the link from the failure WhatsApp/email on your phone, and confirm it is the same page.
Tap 'Change payment method'. On Stripe, enter 4242 4242 4242 4242 and save.
Confirm the page now shows 'Visa ••••4242'.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Check Stripe, Invoices, Payment History and email.
expected: One new successful Stripe charge for the owed balance plus the card fee.
The invoice is 'paid'. Payment History has the new row(s) with Reference 'Visa ••••4242'.
One receipt email. No new failure message.
evidence: Pay page after the change. The Stripe successful payment. The Payment History row. The receipt.

title: Check how cards that require authentication (3-D Secure) are handled
risk: A charge sits half-finished and could later complete alongside another payment (double collection), or fails silently.
preconditions: Stripe is in Test mode.
Two test families with open invoices and autopay off: Parent G1 and Parent G2.
steps: Parent G1: open the pay link, tap 'Card', enter 4000 0025 0000 3155. Complete the authentication pop-up Stripe shows ('Complete').
Parent G2: open the pay link, tap 'Card', enter 4000 0027 6000 3184 (authentication on EVERY payment). Complete the authentication when saving.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Check Stripe, Invoices, the Outbox and email for both families.
expected: G1 (3155): this card was authenticated for later use when saved, so the off-session charge should SUCCEED, giving a 'paid' invoice and a receipt. If it fails instead, record the exact message.
G2 (3184): the charge does NOT complete. In Stripe it is failed, cancelled or incomplete, never 'Succeeded', and it cannot be completed later.
G2's invoice is owed again. One WhatsApp in the Outbox and one failure email, with a reason about the bank asking to confirm or authentication.
G2 is not retried the next day unless a new payment method is saved.
evidence: Stripe payment detail for both families showing the final status. G2's Outbox message and failure email.

title: Turn autopay off from the parent page and confirm charges really stop
risk: A parent who cancelled is still charged, a consumer-protection and chargeback exposure.
preconditions: Test Parent H has autopay on (card 4242) and an open invoice not yet charged (e.g. set up after today's run, or a newly generated invoice).
steps: Open Parent H's pay link on your phone. Tap 'Turn off'.
Check that a confirmation appears with 'Yes, turn off autopay' and 'Keep it on'. Tap 'Keep it on' first and confirm nothing changed.
Tap 'Turn off' again, then 'Yes, turn off autopay'.
Check the page.
In Stripe (Test mode), open Customers → Parent H → Payment methods.
As Boss, check Payments: the 'Autopay' panel count of families who pay automatically.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it. Check Stripe and the invoice.
expected: Turning off takes two taps with no message to anyone. The page returns to 'Pay automatically' with the Bank/Card buttons, and the Zelle section reappears.
The card no longer appears on the Stripe customer (it was detached).
The Autopay panel count drops by one.
The daily run creates NO charge for Parent H, and the invoice stays owed.
evidence: Phone screenshots of the confirm step and the after state. The Stripe customer with no payment method. The Autopay panel count before and after. Stripe payments the next day showing no charge.

title: Change the payment method, and switch between card and bank
risk: The old card is charged after the parent changed it, or a parent cannot move from card (fee) to bank (no fee).
preconditions: Test Parent I has card autopay on (Visa ••••4242) and an open invoice.
steps: On Parent I's payment page, tap 'Change payment method'. Note which Stripe page opens: card form or bank picker.
Save a different test card (e.g. 5555 5555 5555 4444, a Mastercard).
Confirm the page now shows 'Mastercard ••••4444'.

Now try to switch to a bank account: look for any way to choose 'Bank account' while autopay is on. If there is none, tap 'Turn off' → 'Yes, turn off autopay', then tap 'Bank account' and complete Test Institution.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it. Check Stripe.
expected: With autopay on, the page offers both 'Use a different card' (or bank account) and 'Switch to bank (no fee)' / 'Switch to card'. Each opens the matching Stripe form.
After changing, only the new method is shown, and the next charge uses it (Stripe shows the new last 4).
After switching to bank, the charge has no card fee.
evidence: Screenshots of the page before and after each change. The Stripe charge showing which payment method was used.

title: Charge the paying parent when the invoice is billed to the other parent
risk: The wrong parent is charged or chased, or the family is never collected because the invoice names someone else.
preconditions: One child linked to two parents: Mother (the parent named on the invoice in Payments → Invoices 'Parent' column) and Father.
Both have their own pay link and email. Autopay is off for both.
steps: Open FATHER's pay link (copy it from his parent record or ask Mutaaf). Check it shows the child's open invoice under 'To pay'.
Set up card autopay on Father's page with 4242 4242 4242 4242.
Open MOTHER's page and check what it shows.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Check Stripe (which customer was charged), Payment History, and both parents' emails.
Extra (double-charge check): set up autopay on Mother's page too, generate or obtain a new open invoice for the child, and run again.
expected: Father's page shows the child's invoice even though it is billed to Mother.
Mother's page shows the same balance and does not show Father's card details.
Father's Stripe customer is charged once, and the invoice becomes 'paid'. The receipt goes to Father.
With both parents on autopay, the child's invoice is charged ONCE in total, never once per parent.
evidence: Both pay pages. The Invoices row showing the billed parent. The Stripe customer charged. A Stripe list showing a single charge in the both-on case.

title: Check that invalid, altered and forwarded pay links behave safely
risk: A guessed or tampered link reveals another family's page, or lets someone change another family's payment set-up.
preconditions: Two test families (Parent J and Parent K) with working pay links.
steps: Open Parent J's link, then change one character in the last part of the URL and load it.
Delete half of the code after /pay/ and load it.
Load https://app.risingstars.training/pay/ followed by random text.

Forward Parent J's link to a different phone (or open it in a private window, not logged in) and confirm the page loads without a login. Note what someone holding the link could do: turn off autopay, change the receipt email, save a Zelle name.
Set up card autopay for Parent J. When Stripe returns you, copy the whole address bar (it ends in '?setup=cs_…'). Then open Parent K's link and add the same '?setup=cs_…' ending. Load it.
Search Google for the business name plus 'pay' and check no family pages are listed.
expected: Altered, truncated or random links show a 'not found' page. They never show another family and never show an error with technical details.
A forwarded link works for anyone holding it (by design; record this as an accepted control: the link is the key). Saved email is shown only masked (e.g. 'r•••@gmail.com').
Parent K's page is unchanged by Parent J's setup code: autopay stays off, and no Parent J card appears.
No pay pages appear in search results.
evidence: Screenshots of each not-found result. Parent K's page after the cross-family attempt. Notes on what a link holder can change.

title: Audit the payment page for data exposure
risk: A forwarded or screenshotted link leaks children's last names, phone numbers, full bank details or other families' data.
preconditions: A test family with two children, a saved email, a saved card or bank, and at least one Zelle name saved via 'Sending from an account in someone else's name?'.
steps: Open the family's pay link on your phone and read every section top to bottom: header, 'To pay', autopay, Zelle, 'Receipts by email'.
Write down every piece of personal data visible.
Repeat with autopay off (Zelle section visible) and with autopay on.
Try entering another real family's full name in the Zelle 'Name on the account' box and tap 'Save'.
Tap 'Card' and on Stripe's page check what is pre-filled (email, name).
expected: Shown: the parent's FIRST name, children's FIRST names, program names, months, due dates, amounts, the business name, the Zelle recipient, the masked email, and the card/bank label with last 4 only.
NOT shown: any last name of the parent or child, phone numbers, addresses, medical notes, school, other families, full card or bank numbers.
Saved Zelle sender names show as first name and initial only ('We'll recognise: Miguel G.'), never in full.
Saving another family's name is refused: 'That name is already linked to another family. Message us and we'll sort it out.'
Stripe's page shows only what Stripe needs. No other family's data is pre-filled.
evidence: Full-page phone screenshots in both states, with a data inventory list annotated as allowed or not allowed. A screenshot of the refused Zelle name.

title: Check that a Stripe-hosted invoice is voided when autopay charges the same month
risk: A family pays the same month twice: once by the emailed Stripe invoice link and once by autopay.
preconditions: Stripe enabled so that generating invoices also creates Stripe invoices (an external-link icon 'Stripe invoice' appears in the 'Pay link' column).
Test Parent L has an open invoice with a Stripe invoice link, and has just set up card autopay.
steps: On Payments → Invoices, click Parent L's 'Stripe invoice' icon and note that the Stripe page is payable.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it.
Click the same Stripe invoice link again (keep the copied URL), and check the 'Pay link' column.
In Stripe → Invoices, find that invoice.
expected: After the run, the Stripe invoice is 'Void' and cannot be paid.
The 'Stripe invoice' icon no longer shows for that row.
The family is charged once, by autopay only.
evidence: Stripe invoice before (Open) and after (Void). The autopay charge in Stripe. The Invoices row.

title: Bank account verified by micro-deposits ('One last step')
risk: An unverified bank account is debited, or a family thinks autopay is on when it is not.
preconditions: Test family Parent M with an open invoice, autopay off.
steps: Open the pay link, tap 'Bank account'. In Stripe choose to enter details manually: routing 110000000, account 000123456789.
Return to the page.
As Boss, wait for or trigger the daily run, and check Stripe for any charge.
On the pay page tap 'Confirm my bank account' and verify using Stripe's test values (amounts 32 and 45, or code SM11AA).
Reload the pay page, then wait for or trigger the next run.
expected: Before verification the page shows 'One last step — Your bank will show a small deposit from Stripe in 1–2 business days…' with a 'Confirm my bank account' button. It does NOT say 'Autopay is on'.
No charge is made while it is pending, and the family is not counted in the Autopay panel.
After verification the page shows 'Autopay is on'. The next run charges with no fee.
evidence: Screenshot of 'One last step'. Stripe showing no charge while pending. The page after verification. The charge.

title: Check that redelivered Stripe webhooks do not double-book payments or receipts
risk: Stripe resends an event, and the books show a payment twice or the parent gets duplicate receipts, misstating revenue.
preconditions: A successful autopay charge exists from PAY-01, PAY-02 or PAY-03.
Access to the Stripe dashboard (Test mode) → Developers → Webhooks (or Workbench → Webhooks).
steps: In Stripe, open the CoachOS webhook endpoint and find the 'payment_intent.succeeded' event for that charge.
Note the Payment History rows for that charge and the number of receipt emails.
Click 'Resend' on the event. Confirm the delivery shows a 200 response.
Refresh Payments → Payment History and check email.
Repeat for a 'payment_intent.payment_failed' event from PAY-06.
expected: Resending returns success (200).
No new Payment History row, and totals unchanged ('Total Revenue', 'Paid This Month').
No second receipt email, and no second failure WhatsApp or email.
evidence: Stripe webhook delivery log showing the resend and 200. Payment History before and after. The inbox showing a single receipt.

title: Reconcile Stripe against CoachOS Payment History and receipts for a period
risk: Revenue reported in CoachOS does not match money collected in Stripe, so fees are mis-accounted and errors go undetected.
preconditions: Several test autopay charges completed (card single, card siblings, bank, at least one failure).
steps: In Stripe (Test mode) → Payments, filter to the test period and export or list every succeeded charge: amount, Stripe fee and net, description, customer.
In CoachOS Payments → Payment History, filter Method 'stripe' and list each row: date, student, amount, reference. Open each row's edit to read Notes for 'card fee $X'.
For each Stripe charge, match the CoachOS rows (one per child/invoice) and the receipt email.
Compute: Stripe gross = sum of CoachOS amounts + sum of card fees in Notes = receipt 'Total'.
Check that failed Stripe charges have NO CoachOS payment row.
Compare the CoachOS 'Paid This Month' card with your sum.
expected: Every succeeded Stripe charge maps to one or more CoachOS rows and exactly one receipt. Nothing is unmatched in either direction.
Gross ties out to the cent, including card-fee rounding per invoice.

Note for the report: the CoachOS Amount column EXCLUDES the card fee, which is recorded only in Notes (and as a separate fee field). Stripe's own processing fee (Stripe's fee and net) is not recorded in CoachOS at all. Flag this if the business needs net revenue.
No payment rows exist for failed or cancelled charges.
evidence: A reconciliation worksheet (Stripe charge ID ↔ CoachOS rows ↔ receipt). Screenshots of any exception.

title: Stripe mode switch: check the connection, switch Test → Live with confirmation, and review the effect on test-set-up families
risk: Live mode is switched on with the wrong keys or account, or families keep 'autopay on' pointing at cards that don't exist in Live and silently fail every month.
preconditions: The new Settings → Payments 'Stripe mode' switch is deployed. Separate test and live keys are entered (Mutaaf to provide live keys or do the live part with you).
At least two test families have autopay on (set up in Test mode).
Agree with Mutaaf a window when no daily run will happen, and do NOT leave Live on through a daily run.
steps: Settings → Payments: with mode Test, click 'Check connection'. Note the account name and mode it reports and compare them with the Stripe dashboard account name (top-left) in Test mode.
Enter a deliberately wrong test key (e.g. delete a character), save, and click 'Check connection'. Then restore the correct key.
Optional control test: paste a LIVE key into the TEST key field and click 'Check connection'.
Note the Payments 'Autopay' panel count of families paying automatically.
Switch the mode to Live. When the confirmation appears, cancel it first and confirm nothing changed. Then switch again and confirm.
Click 'Check connection' in Live.
Look at the Autopay panel count and open one of the test families' pay pages.
Switch back to Test straight away (see PAY-19).
expected: 'Check connection' names the Stripe account and mode, matching the dashboard.
A wrong key gives a clear failure message, not a false 'connected'.
A live key in the test field is rejected or clearly flagged as the wrong mode (if it is accepted silently, record it as an exception).
Switching needs explicit confirmation, and cancelling leaves the mode unchanged.

After switching to Live: families set up in Test have autopay turned OFF. Their pay pages show 'Pay automatically' with the Bank/Card buttons again, and the Autopay panel count drops to 0 (or to the live-set-up families only).
No charge is attempted in Live against any test-mode card.
evidence: Screenshots of Check connection in both modes next to the Stripe dashboard account name. The confirmation dialog. The Autopay panel count before and after. A family pay page after the switch.

title: Stripe mode switch Live → Test: families set up in Live are turned off, and webhooks from both modes are accepted
risk: Switching back leaves live-card families pointing at the wrong mode, or webhooks from one mode are rejected so real payments are never booked.
preconditions: PAY-18 done and the mode is Live.
Optional, and only with Mutaaf's agreement: one internal family (e.g. Mutaaf's own) set up autopay in Live with a real card. Turn it off before any daily run unless a real charge is intended.
steps: In Live, if agreed, set up autopay on the internal family's pay page and confirm it shows 'Autopay is on'.
Switch the mode back to Test and confirm.
Check the internal family's pay page and the Autopay panel count.
Click 'Check connection' and confirm it reports Test mode.
In the Stripe dashboard TEST webhooks, resend a recent event (e.g. checkout.session.completed) and confirm the response is 200.
If live webhooks are configured, check Stripe LIVE → Webhooks: recent deliveries show 200, not 400 'Invalid signature'.
Have a test family set up a card again in Test mode (4242) and let the next run charge it.
expected: After switching to Test, the family set up in Live has autopay turned off and must set up again.
Test-mode families previously turned off in PAY-18 stay off until they set up again. They are not silently re-enabled with stale cards.
Webhook deliveries from both Test and Live endpoints are accepted (200).
A fresh Test setup charges normally (as in PAY-01).
evidence: Pay page screenshots after the switch back. Stripe webhook delivery logs for both modes. The Check connection result.

title: Check that a family who sets up mid-month is charged the next day, and only once
risk: New autopay families wait a month to be charged, or a repeated run charges them twice.
preconditions: Test Parent N has an open invoice for this month (due on the 1st, so already due) and autopay off.
steps: Open Parent N's pay link and read the small print under the buttons: 'Your current balance of $X will be paid within a day. After that, each month's fee is paid on its due date (the 1st).'
Set up card 4242.
Wait for the next daily run, or ask Mutaaf to trigger it. Then ask Mutaaf to trigger it a SECOND time the same day.
Check Stripe and Payment History.
expected: $X on the page equals the 'To pay' total.
Exactly one Stripe charge after the first run. The second run adds no charge and no new Payment History row.
The invoice is 'paid' and one receipt is sent.
evidence: Pay page small print. A Stripe payments list showing a single charge after two runs. Payment History.

title: Set up the Gmail script once and confirm it connects
risk: If the script is missing, installed in the wrong Gmail, or holds the wrong key, no Zelle payment is recorded automatically and families look unpaid. Nothing in the app warns that payments have stopped arriving.
preconditions: You are signed in to https://app.risingstars.training on a computer, not a phone. Google's script editor does not work on a phone.
You know the password for the Gmail account that will receive the forwarded alerts.
In Settings, 'Zelle Number or Email' shows her phone number and her Yahoo address, separated by a comma.
steps: Go to Settings. Find 'Zelle Alerts Gmail' and enter the Gmail address. Find 'Bank Alerts Arrive At' and enter the Yahoo address. Save.
Look at 'Zelle Email Key'. It should show dots, not readable text. Do not change it.
Scroll to the 'Zelle email setup' section. Confirm step 1 reads 'Open Gmail as <the Gmail you entered>' and step 5 reads 'From now on, forward Zelle alerts from <the Yahoo address>'.
Click 'Open Gmail' and check that the Gmail that opens is the right account, not another Google account you are signed in to.

Optional cross-check: go to Payments. The Zelle card's button should now read 'Setup' instead of 'Connect Gmail', but only once at least one email containing the word 'zelle' has been posted. Before that, the card keeps saying 'Connect the Gmail your bank emails...'.

expected: Every address in the setup steps matches what you saved in Settings, with nothing typed by hand.
The key is never shown in readable form on screen. It can only be copied.
Exactly one 15-minute trigger exists, whichever function was run. Pressing Run again does not add a second one.
After the first Zelle email is processed, the Payments page shows the Zelle card as connected ('Setup' button).
evidence: Screenshots of the Settings fields (key masked), the setup steps showing the correct addresses, the Apps Script Triggers list showing one trigger, and the Payments Zelle card before and after it connects.

title: Record a real $1 Zelle from a known parent automatically
risk: If an exact, unambiguous payment is not recorded by itself, the time-saving control fails and families are chased for money they already paid. If it records against the wrong invoice, the ledger is wrong.
preconditions: ZEL-01 passed.
You have a test family whose parent's first and last name exactly match the name on a cooperating sender's bank account (for example 'Sam Rivera'). The parent's email is an inbox you can read.
That family has exactly one open invoice, edited to $1.00 under Payments → Invoices, with status Pending or Overdue.
Note the family's invoice status and the Payments → Payment History count before you start.
steps: Have the sender Zelle exactly $1.00 to her phone number or Yahoo address, with the memo 'TEST ZEL-02'.
On your phone, open the Yahoo inbox, find the bank's 'sent you $1.00' alert, and forward it unchanged to the Zelle Alerts Gmail. Note the time.
Wait up to 20 minutes, then open Payments.
On the Zelle card, expand 'Recently recorded' and find the entry.
Open Payments → Invoices and find the test family's invoice.
Open Payments → Payment History and find the new row.
Check the parent's inbox for a receipt.
expected: The payment does not appear under 'to check'. It appears under 'Recently recorded' as '<date> · Sam Rivera $1.00'.
The invoice status changes to Paid.
Payment History has exactly one new row: Method Zelle, Amount $1.00, Reference 'Zelle from Sam Rivera', for the correct student.
The date recorded is the day the forwarded alert reached Gmail. Note any difference from the bank's own date.
Exactly one receipt email arrives from payments@risingstars.training (see EML-01 for the content checks).
evidence: Screenshots of the bank alert (with timestamp), the forwarded email, the 'Recently recorded' entry, the invoice showing Paid, the Payment History row, and the receipt email. Record the elapsed time from forwarding to recording.

title: Match a spouse's payment by hand, then confirm the next one matches by itself
risk: Payments from an account in another name could be lost, or recorded against the wrong family. A learned name that does not stick means the same manual work every month.
preconditions: There is a test family with two open $1.00 invoices in different months.
A cooperating sender's bank-account name does not match any parent on file (for example a spouse, 'Jordan Rivera').
Nobody has registered that name on the family's payment page.
steps: Have the spouse Zelle $1.00, then forward the alert to the Zelle Alerts Gmail.
Within 20 minutes, open Payments. On the Zelle card, find the badge 'N to check'.
Read the entry: the sender name, the amount, the memo, and the amber note.
In the 'Who sent this?' dropdown, choose the test family (shown as 'Parent Name (Child names)'), then click Record.
Check Payments → Invoices and Payment History.
Expand 'Recently recorded' and look at the entry.
Next, have the same spouse Zelle another $1.00 and forward the alert.
expected: The first payment is not recorded automatically. The note reads 'No parent on file is called Jordan Rivera — it may be a spouse or another account.'
The Record button stays disabled until a family is chosen.
After Record, you see the message 'Payment recorded', the entry leaves the to-check list, and the oldest $1.00 invoice becomes Paid.
'Recently recorded' shows 'Jordan Rivera $1.00 → <Parent First Last>'.
The second payment from Jordan Rivera is recorded automatically against the remaining invoice, with no to-check entry, and a receipt goes to the family.
evidence: Screenshots of the to-check entry with its note, the dropdown selection, the 'Payment recorded' message, the Recently recorded entry with the arrow to the family, and the second payment recorded automatically.

title: A parent registers a different account name on their payment page, and cannot claim another family's
risk: If the alias does not work, parents' payments pile up for manual review. If a parent can claim another family's name, someone else's payments could be credited to the wrong family.
preconditions: There are test families A and B. Family A has an open $1.00 invoice and autopay is not active.
'Zelle Number or Email' is set in Settings.
You know the full name of family B's parent.
steps: Go to Payments → Invoices. On family A's row, click the link icon ('Copy this family's payment page link') and open the link on your phone.
In the 'Pay with Zelle' (or 'Prefer Zelle?') section, confirm both Zelle targets show, each with its own Copy button, separated by 'or'.
Under 'Sending from an account in someone else's name?', type a single word (for example 'Grandma') and press Save.
Type the full name on the cooperating sender's account (for example 'Pat Lee') and press Save.
Type family B's parent's full name and press Save.
Have Pat Lee Zelle $1.00 and forward the alert.
expected: The single word is rejected with: 'Please enter the first and last name on the account.'
The real name saves with 'Saved — thank you.', and the page shows 'We'll recognise: Pat Lee' (or similar).
Family B's name is rejected with: 'That name is already linked to another family. Message us and we'll sort it out.'
Family A's page never shows family B's name, children or amounts.
Pat Lee's $1.00 is recorded automatically against family A, with no manual step.
evidence: Phone screenshots of each message on the payment page, the 'We'll recognise' line, and the automatic recording in 'Recently recorded' (showing '→ Family A parent').

title: An amount that does not match what is owed is never recorded automatically
risk: If the system guesses which invoice an odd amount pays, money is posted to the wrong month or child and the ledger cannot be trusted. The control is: no guessing.
preconditions: There is a known test parent (exact name match) with one open invoice of $2.00.
A second known test parent has no open invoices.
steps: Have the first parent Zelle $1.00 (less than the $2.00 owed) and forward the alert.
Within 20 minutes, open Payments and look at the Zelle card.
Check that invoice's status and Payment History.
Have the second parent (who owes nothing) Zelle $1.00 and forward the alert.
Look at the Zelle card again.
For the first entry, choose the family in 'Who sent this?' and click Record. Check the invoice afterwards.

The first entry shows the note '$1.00 doesn't match what this family owes ($2.00 open).', and the family is already pre-selected in the dropdown as a suggestion.
The second entry shows 'This family has nothing open to pay.'

If you try Record for the family with nothing open, you see 'That family has nothing open to pay. Generate this month's invoices first, or ignore this one.'
evidence: Screenshots of both to-check entries with their notes, Payment History before and after, and the invoice balance after the manual record.

title: Two parents with the same name are never auto-matched
risk: A payment from one 'Maria Lopez' could be credited to the other family with the same name.
preconditions: There are two test families whose parents share a first and last name with the cooperating sender's bank-account name (for example two parents called 'Maria Lopez').
Both families have an open $1.00 invoice.
Neither family has registered that name on its payment page.
steps: Have Maria Lopez Zelle $1.00 and forward the alert.
Within 20 minutes, open Payments → Zelle card.
Open the 'Who sent this?' dropdown and confirm you can tell the two families apart.
Choose the correct family and click Record.
Check both families' invoices.
expected: The payment waits in the to-check list with the note 'More than one parent is called Maria Lopez.' Nothing is recorded automatically.
The dropdown shows both families with their children's names in brackets, so they can be told apart.
Only the chosen family's invoice becomes Paid. The other family's invoice is unchanged.

Known behaviour to confirm: after Record, the name is remembered for the chosen family, so the next Maria Lopez payment auto-matches to that family. Decide whether that is acceptable when the other Maria Lopez might also pay. If not, log it as an exception.
evidence: Screenshots of the note, the dropdown showing both families, and both invoices after recording. Record what happens with a second payment from the same name.

title: One Zelle covering two siblings pays both invoices with one receipt
risk: A combined payment for siblings could be left unmatched, or applied to only one child, leaving the other wrongly overdue and chased.
preconditions: There is a known test parent (exact name) with two children enrolled, each with an open $1.00 invoice for the same month.
steps: Have the parent Zelle exactly $2.00 and forward the alert.
Within 20 minutes, check the Zelle card, Payments → Invoices and Payments → Payment History.
Open the receipt email in the parent's inbox.
expected: The payment is recorded automatically. Both invoices become Paid.
Payment History shows two rows of $1.00, one per child, both with Reference 'Zelle from <name>'.
Exactly one receipt email arrives, listing both children, with a Total of $2.00.
evidence: Screenshots of both invoices showing Paid, the two Payment History rows, and the single receipt.

title: A payment for one month pays the oldest month first
risk: If the newer month is paid first, the older month goes overdue and the family is chased for a month they consider paid.
preconditions: There is a known test parent with two open $1.00 invoices for the same child, for two different months (for example August and September).
steps: Have the parent Zelle $1.00 and forward the alert.
Within 20 minutes, open Payments → Invoices and look at both invoices.
Check the receipt email.
expected: It is recorded automatically. The older month (August) becomes Paid and the newer month (September) stays open.
The receipt names the older month.
evidence: Screenshots of both invoices after recording, and the receipt line showing the month.

title: An overpayment is noted, not lost
risk: Extra money received but not shown anywhere cannot be refunded or carried forward, and the books will not reconcile to the bank.
preconditions: There is a known test parent with exactly one open $1.00 invoice.
steps: Have the parent Zelle $2.00 and forward the alert.
Within 20 minutes, confirm it waits on the Zelle card with a 'doesn't match' note.
Choose the family in 'Who sent this?' and click Record.
Look everywhere the extra $1.00 could appear: the confirmation message, the 'Recently recorded' entry, Payments → Invoices, and Payment History.
Check the receipt email total.
expected: Nothing is recorded automatically. The note reads '$2.00 doesn't match what this family owes ($1.00 open).'
After Record, the $1.00 invoice is Paid and Payment History shows $1.00.
The extra $1.00 must be visible somewhere you can act on (the intended note is '$1.00 more than was owed — not applied to anything.').
The surplus is visible: the 'Recently recorded' entry shows the note '$1.00 more than was owed — not applied to anything.' in amber, so the extra can be refunded or carried forward.
The receipt shows $1.00, not $2.00. Note whether the parent is told about the extra $1.00.
evidence: Screenshots of every place checked for the surplus, Payment History, and the receipt. Record the bank amount against the recorded amount.

title: Undo a wrong match: payments removed and the name forgotten
risk: A wrong match that cannot be reversed leaves one family credited and another chased. A name that is still remembered repeats the error every month.
preconditions: There are test families X and Y, each with an open $1.00 invoice.
A cooperating sender's name is unknown to the system.
steps: Have the sender Zelle $1.00 and forward the alert. On the Zelle card, deliberately choose the wrong family (X) and click Record.
Expand 'Recently recorded'. On that entry, click the circular-arrow undo icon at the right. Note that it has no text label.
Read the confirmation box ('Remove this payment and put it back in the inbox?') and click OK.
Check family X's invoice and Payment History.
Look at the to-check list.
Now record it to the correct family (Y).
Optional: before recording to Y, have the same sender send another $1.00 and see whether it auto-matches to X.
Check family X's parent inbox.
expected: After undo, you see 'Moved back to the inbox'. Family X's invoice reverts to Pending or Overdue, and the Payment History row is gone.
The entry is back in the to-check list with the note 'Match undone — pick the right family.'
A further payment from that sender is not auto-matched to X, because the name has been forgotten.
After recording to Y, only Y's invoice is Paid.

Control gap to record: family X already received a receipt email for money that was not theirs, and no correction email is sent. Note this as a known exception that needs a manual message to family X.
Note also: 'Recently recorded' only lists the last 8 matched payments, so an older wrong match cannot be undone from this card.
evidence: Screenshots before and after undo (invoice status, Payment History, to-check entry with note), the wrong receipt in family X's inbox, and the final correct recording.

title: 'Not a family' removes an unrelated payment without recording anything
risk: Personal money (a friend paying back lunch) could be recorded as tuition, or a real payment could be dismissed by mistake with no way back.
preconditions: A cooperating sender is unknown to the system and is not a parent.
steps: Have them Zelle $1.00 with the memo 'lunch' and forward the alert.
On the Zelle card, find the entry and confirm the memo shows in quotes.
Click 'Not a family'.
Check the to-check count, 'Recently recorded', Invoices and Payment History.
Try to find the dismissed entry anywhere in the app.
expected: The entry disappears from the to-check list and the count drops by one.
No payment is created and no invoice changes. No email is sent to anyone.

Record as an observation: a dismissed entry cannot be seen or restored from the app (there is no confirmation prompt and no 'dismissed' list). A misclick on a real payment would need it recorded by hand using Record Payment.
evidence: Screenshots before and after clicking, and of Payment History showing no new row.

title: Her own outgoing Zelle and Zelle requests never appear
risk: Money she sent out could be recorded as income from a family, overstating collections.
preconditions: ZEL-01 passed. You have access to her Zelle so you can send $1.00 out and request $1.00.
steps: From her bank, Zelle $1.00 to someone (a cooperating person).
From her bank, request $1.00 from someone.
Forward both bank emails ('You sent...', 'You requested...') from Yahoo to the Zelle Alerts Gmail.
Wait 30 minutes (two script runs). Check the Zelle card, 'Recently recorded', and Payment History.
expected: Neither email appears anywhere: not in the to-check list, not as unreadable, not in 'Recently recorded', and not in Payment History.
An INCOMING alert whose subject mentions a request (e.g. 'Payment request paid: <name> sent you $1.00') is still recorded as income: incoming wording is checked before outgoing.
evidence: Screenshots of the two forwarded emails in Gmail (with timestamps) and the Zelle card and Payment History 30 minutes later showing nothing new.

title: Duplicate control: the same alert is never recorded twice
risk: A payment recorded twice understates what a family owes and overstates collections, and the family gets two receipts.
preconditions: There is a known test parent with two open $1.00 invoices (so a duplicate would have somewhere to land).
steps: Have the parent Zelle $1.00 and forward the alert once.
Wait at least 45 minutes (three script runs, each of which re-sends the last 3 days of emails). Check Payment History and the parent's inbox.
Now forward the same original bank alert to the Gmail a second time (a re-forward, as might happen by accident).
Wait 20 minutes. Check the Zelle card, Invoices, Payment History, and the parent's inbox.
expected: After the repeated script runs, there is exactly one payment row, one Paid invoice and one receipt.
After the re-forward, there should be no second payment.

The re-forward is NOT recorded a second time. It waits in the to-check list with the note 'Looks like a repeat of the $1.00 from <name> on <date>, which is already recorded. Record it only if this is a second payment.' A genuine second payment from the same person within a week also waits here for one tap.
evidence: Payment History screenshots after each stage, the count of receipts in the parent's inbox, and both forwarded emails in Gmail.

title: Unreadable or odd emails are kept visible, not dropped
risk: A real payment in a format the system cannot read could vanish silently, leaving a family wrongly overdue.
preconditions: ZEL-01 passed.
steps: From any email account, send the Zelle Alerts Gmail an email with the subject 'Zelle question' and the body 'Did my Zelle go through?' (no amount, no 'sent you').
Forward a bank alert after editing it so that the amount is removed. Use the subject 'Fwd: Zelle payment'.
Wait 20 minutes and open Payments → Zelle card.
Read each entry, then try the buttons available.
expected: Each email appears in the to-check list, titled with its subject (or 'An email we couldn't read'), with the note 'Couldn't find a sender and amount in this email. If it's a payment, record it by hand.'
Unreadable entries offer only 'Dismiss'. There is no family dropdown and no Record button.
No payment or email to a parent is created.

Note: the Gmail script only picks up emails containing the word 'zelle' from the last 3 days. An alert that does not mention Zelle, or one forwarded more than 3 days late, will never reach the app. Record this as a limitation.
evidence: Screenshots of the test emails in Gmail and of the unreadable entries on the Zelle card.

title: Changing the alert addresses or the Zelle Email Key in Settings takes effect immediately
risk: Stale setup instructions send alerts to the wrong inbox. A leaked key that cannot be revoked lets anyone put fake payments in front of the owner.
preconditions: ZEL-01 passed. Schedule this when no real payments are expected, because it briefly stops automatic recording.
steps: In Settings, change 'Bank Alerts Arrive At' to a different test address and save. Without refreshing anything else, open Payments → Zelle card → 'Setup' and read step 5. Also read the 'Zelle email setup' section in Settings.
Change it back and save.
In Settings, change 'Zelle Email Key' to a new value and save. Do not update the Apps Script.
Have a known parent Zelle $1.00 and forward the alert. Wait 20 minutes.
Check the Zelle card and Payment History. In Apps Script, open Executions and look at the latest run.
Now copy the script again (step 3, 'Copy the script'), paste it over the old one in Apps Script, save, and press Run.
Wait 20 minutes and check again.
expected: Step 5 and the Settings setup section show the new address straight after saving.
While the old key is in the script, the $1.00 is not recorded. Apps Script shows a failed or unauthorised request.
After pasting the new script, the waiting payment is recorded automatically, because the script re-sends the last 3 days, and it is recorded once only.

The Zelle card shows 'Gmail script checked in N min ago'. If the script stops (e.g. the key no longer matches), within about 40 minutes it changes to an amber warning: 'The Gmail script last checked in … ago, so it has stopped checking.'
evidence: Screenshots of the setup steps before and after the change, the Apps Script execution showing failure and then success, and Payment History showing a single recording.

title: A Zelle from a brand-new family creates the family, child, school and program together, and records the money
risk: A payment from someone not yet set up sits unrecorded, or is forced onto the wrong family. A half-finished setup leaves a parent with no child, or a child with no program, who is then never billed.
preconditions: Test mode. A Zelle receipt from a sender not on file (ask Mutaaf to add one, or Zelle $1 from an account whose name isn't a parent's).
Pick a school name and program name that don't exist yet, e.g. 'Audit School' / 'Audit Program'.
steps: On Payments, in the Zelle box, tap 'Who paid this?' on the payment.
Tap 'Someone new'. Note the name filled in from the Zelle sender.
Enter a test phone number and tap 'Next: their child'. Enter a child first name.
Choose '+ A new school' and type the school name. Type the program name; note the monthly fee filled in.
Tap 'Next: check it over' and read every line. Then tap 'Record'.
Open Schools, then Students, and find what was added. Open Payments → Invoices.
expected: The parent's name is filled in from the sender, without a middle initial.
The fee starts at the amount paid.
The summary lists the new family, new school, new program with its fee, the child being added, and whether the month is paid in full — before anything is saved.
After Record: the school, program, parent and child all exist and are linked; this month's invoice exists for the child at the program's fee and shows paid (or the remaining balance).
The Zelle payment leaves the 'to check' list and appears under Recently recorded with the family's name.
A second Zelle from the same sender records itself without asking.
evidence: Screenshots of the summary screen and of the resulting invoice; the school and student pages.

title: 'Who paid this?' never makes a duplicate family, school or program, and saves nothing if a step is missing
risk: Duplicate families split a household's invoices and payments, so balances look wrong and parents are chased twice. A partial save leaves records that are never billed.
preconditions: A test family on file with a known phone number and a child in a program.
steps: On Payments, tap 'Record Payment' (top right), enter an amount and choose Cash.
Tap 'Someone new' and type the test family's phone number in a different format (e.g. with dots).
Read the yellow message, then use the button offered.
Close and start again: 'Record Payment' → 'Someone new', a new phone number, a child name, '+ A new school' with the name of an EXISTING school typed in capitals. Continue to the summary and record.
Start again with a new program but leave the monthly fee empty, and try to continue.
expected: Typing an existing phone shows whose number it is and offers that family; 'Next' stays disabled until you use it.
Using the offered family goes on with that family — no second parent is created.
A 'new' school typed with an existing name in different capitals uses the existing school; Schools shows no duplicate.
With no fee, 'Next' stays disabled and nothing is created.
Payments shows the cash payment with method Cash.
evidence: Screenshots of the yellow duplicate warning and of the Schools list afterwards.

title: Receipt content agrees with Payment History and never shows another family
risk: A receipt with the wrong amount, child or fee misleads parents and their employers or tax records. A receipt showing another family's data is a privacy breach.
preconditions: Settings → 'Email Parents' is on.
There are test families with email addresses you can read: one paid by Zelle (ZEL-02 or ZEL-07), one paid by card through autopay if Stripe is on, and one paid by cash.
For the cash payment: go to Payments, click 'Record Payment' on a test family's invoice row, enter Cash and the amount, and save.
steps: Open each receipt email. Note the sender, the subject, the heading, each line (child · month, program, amount), any 'Card processing fee' line, the Total, 'Paid by ... on ...', and the 'View your payment page' button.
For each, open Payments → Payment History and filter to that student. Compare the date, the amount per child, and the method.
Click 'View your payment page' in the receipt and check whose page opens.
Check that each receipt lists only that family's own children, even when another family paid the same day.
expected: Sender: payments@risingstars.training (shown as 'Rising Stars'). Subject: 'Receipt: $X.XX received — Rising Stars Youth Academy' (or the current Business Name).
Each line's amount equals the matching Payment History row. Total = sum of lines + fee.
A 'Card processing fee' line appears only for card payments, never for Zelle or cash, and it matches the fee charged.
'Paid by Zelle', 'Paid by cash' or the card/bank label is correct, and the date matches Payment History (Dallas time).
The payment-page button opens that family's own page only.
No receipt mentions another family's child, amount or name.
evidence: A side-by-side screenshot of each receipt and its Payment History rows, plus a short reconciliation table: receipt total against recorded total against bank amount.

title: A failed automatic payment emails the family once
risk: If a declined autopay goes unnoticed by the family, the invoice ages into overdue. Duplicate notices erode trust.
preconditions: Stripe is on.
There is a test family with two children on autopay, using a card you can lock or that will decline (for example a virtual card set to a $0 limit), and with an email you can read.
Both children have invoices due.
steps: Lock the card before the next automatic charge run (the daily run, or the 1st of the month).
After the run, check the family's inbox and Messaging → Outbox.
Check Payments → Invoices for both children.
Wait for the next day's run and check the inbox again.
expected: One email (not one per child) with the subject 'Your automatic payment didn't go through — <Business Name>'. It names both children, the total amount owed, and a short reason, and has an 'Update payment' button that opens that family's payment page.
A matching message is waiting in the Outbox to send by WhatsApp.
No second failed-payment email is sent for the same failure on the following day.
No receipt is sent.
evidence: A screenshot of the email, the Outbox message, and the invoices. Note the count of emails received after two daily runs.

title: The overdue reminder goes once (not daily) and once per family
risk: Daily or per-child reminders annoy paying families. Missing reminders leave money uncollected.
preconditions: In Settings, 'Payment Reminders' is on and 'Payment Reminder Delay (days)' is noted (default 3).
There is a test family with two children, each with an unpaid invoice whose due date is more than the delay ago, plus an email address and a phone number.
steps: After the next daily automatic run (early afternoon, Dallas time), check the family's inbox and Messaging → Outbox.
Check the email's subject, lines and total against Payments → Invoices.
Leave the invoices unpaid. Check the inbox and Outbox again after the next two daily runs.
expected: Exactly one email with the subject 'Payment reminder: $X.XX — <Business Name>' and the heading 'A friendly payment reminder'. It lists both children with their month and amount still owed (net of any partial payments), has a 'Pay now' button, and the line 'If you've already sent it, thank you — please ignore this.'
Exactly one Outbox reminder message for the family, covering both children.
No further reminder email or Outbox message on the following days for the same invoices.
A family whose invoice is processing (bank debit under way) or paid is not reminded.
evidence: Inbox screenshots showing one reminder over three days, the Outbox entry, and the invoices showing the amounts owed.

title: Parent replies land in the configured inbox, and changing it takes effect at once
risk: Parent questions sent by replying to a receipt go to an unmonitored address and are never answered.
preconditions: Settings → 'Replies Go To' is set to the address she monitors.
A test family's email is an inbox you control.
steps: Trigger a receipt for the test family (for example 'Record Payment' on an invoice row → cash $1.00).
Open the receipt in the family's inbox and press Reply. Note the 'To' address, then send 'TEST EML-04 reply'.
Confirm it arrives in the 'Replies Go To' inbox and not at payments@risingstars.training.
In Settings, change 'Replies Go To' to a second test address and save.
Immediately trigger another receipt (another $1.00 cash) and reply to it.
Change 'Replies Go To' back to the correct address.
expected: Reply 1 is addressed to, and arrives at, the original 'Replies Go To' address.
Reply 2 (after the change, with no other action) is addressed to the new address.
Earlier emails keep their original reply address, which is expected.
Observation: if 'Replies Go To' is blank or not a valid email, replies go to the sender address. Confirm whether anyone reads that mailbox.

title: Families without email get nothing by email but still get the Outbox message; the master switch works
risk: An error for a family with no email could block their payment being recorded or drop their reminder. A disabled switch that still sends emails breaches the owner's choice.
preconditions: There is a test family with a phone number but no email, and an overdue invoice past the reminder delay.
There is a second test family with an email.
steps: For the no-email family, record a $1.00 cash payment against a different open invoice, using 'Record Payment' on that invoice's row (Payments → Invoices).
After the next daily run, check Messaging → Outbox for a reminder to the no-email family.
Open the no-email family's payment page (link icon on the Invoices row) and check the 'Receipts by email' section.
In Settings, turn 'Email Parents' off and save. Record a $1.00 cash payment for the family with email. Check their inbox.
Turn 'Email Parents' back on.
