Their reminder appears in the Outbox even though no email can go.
Their payment page offers 'Receipts by email', with the text 'Get a receipt whenever a payment comes in...', and entering an address saves with 'Saved — receipts will go there.'
With 'Email Parents' off, no receipt arrives, but the payment is still recorded.
Note: an email skipped while the switch was off is not sent later when it is turned back on.
evidence: Screenshots of the recorded payment, the Outbox reminder, the payment-page email section, the Settings toggle, and the inbox showing no receipt while it was off.

title: Open a message in WhatsApp and in Messages (Text) and confirm it reaches the right parent with the full text intact
risk: A parent gets a cut-off message, a broken payment link, or a message meant for another family, and money or trust is lost.
preconditions: Use a test family only: a test parent whose mobile number is a phone you hold (10-digit US number), linked to a test child enrolled in a test program.
WhatsApp is installed on your phone and WhatsApp Web or WhatsApp Desktop is signed in on your computer.
The Outbox has no real parent messages you might open by accident (check Messaging > Outbox first).
For the Text check: an iPhone with Messages, logged in to the app in Safari (and an Android phone if available).
steps: Go to Messaging > Compose. Click By Program and choose the test program. Confirm only the test parent's name appears as a recipient chip.
In the message box type exactly, on two lines: 'Test 1 — Tom & Jerry's fees: https://app.risingstars.training/pay/test?a=1&b=2' then on a new line 'Thanks & see you Tuesday! 50% off? #3 ⚽'.
Click 'Send to 1 recipient(s)'. Note the toast.
Open the Outbox tab. Find the card for the test parent and tap the message text to expand it. Compare the name and phone shown on the card with the parent's record.
On the computer, click WhatsApp. Before you press send, compare the prefilled text with what you typed, character by character. Then send it.
Repeat steps 1–5 on your phone (log in to the app in the phone browser), tapping WhatsApp on the card.
Create the same message again (steps 1–3). On the iPhone, open Messaging > Outbox and tap Text on the card. Before you send, check the recipient and the full body, then send and return to Safari.
Repeat the Text check on Android if available.
expected: Toast reads '1 message(s) ready in the Outbox'.
The Outbox card shows the test parent's name, their number in readable format, and the full two-line message.
WhatsApp opens a chat with exactly the test parent's number (not a different number, and not a 'number not on WhatsApp' error for a valid number).
The prefilled text is identical. Nothing is lost after either '&', the link keeps '?a=1&b=2', and the apostrophe, '%', '#', line break and emoji all survive.
Tapping the link in the received WhatsApp message opens the same address that was typed.
Text on the iPhone opens Messages addressed to the test parent's number with the complete body pre-filled, including everything after each '&' and the line break.
Back in the app, the Text card sits under 'Sent or skipped today' marked '· by text'. The WhatsApp one is marked '· on WhatsApp'.
evidence: Screenshot the expanded Outbox card and the WhatsApp compose screen before sending, side by side, on both computer and phone. Screenshot the received message on the test phone. Make a screen recording on the iPhone from tapping Text to returning to the app.

title: Check that opening a message marks it sent, and that Undo fully reverses it
risk: Messages are recorded as sent when they were never sent, or an Undo leaves a false entry in the message history, so the record of who was told what is unreliable.
preconditions: At least two pending test messages in the Outbox, addressed to test parents.
Note the counts shown under the Messaging heading ('N sent', 'N pending') and the number on the Outbox tab before starting.
steps: Click WhatsApp on the first test message, then close WhatsApp WITHOUT pressing send.
Return to the app. Note where the message now appears and the counts.
Open the History tab and look for the message.
Back on Outbox, under 'Sent or skipped today', click Undo next to that message.
Refresh the page. Check the Outbox list, the counts and the History tab again.
Click WhatsApp on the same message a second time, send it for real, return, and check History again.
expected: After step 1 the message moves straight to 'Sent or skipped today' with a tick and '· on WhatsApp', even though nothing was sent. This is by design because the app cannot see whether send was pressed. Record it as a control limitation: 'sent' means 'opened', not 'delivered'.
History shows one 'sent' entry for that message.
After Undo and refresh, the message is back in the waiting list, the History entry is gone, and the counts return to their starting values.
After the second, real send there is exactly one History entry, not two.
evidence: Screenshots of the Outbox and History tab at each of the four stages, with the counts visible.

title: Skip one message, then Skip all, and confirm nothing is sent or logged
risk: Messages queued by mistake are sent, or Skip all wipes real parent messages the owner still needed to send.
preconditions: IMPORTANT: Skip all skips EVERY waiting message in the Outbox, not just test ones. Run this only when the Outbox holds nothing but test messages, or agree it with the owner first.
At least three pending test messages (create them through Compose to the test program, sending twice if needed).
steps: On Outbox, click Skip on one test message.
Check where it appears, and whether it appears in the History tab.
Click Undo on the skipped message and confirm it returns to the waiting list.
With two or more messages waiting, click Skip all. Read the confirmation box and click Cancel first. Confirm nothing changed.
Click Skip all again and confirm.
Refresh the page and check Outbox and History.
expected: A skipped message appears under 'Sent or skipped today' marked '· skipped' with no tick, and it is NOT in History.
Undo returns it to the waiting list.
Skip all is offered only when more than one message is waiting. It asks 'Skip all N messages without sending them?', where N equals the waiting count.
Cancel leaves everything as it was. Confirming empties the waiting list ('Nothing to send') and adds nothing to History.
No WhatsApp or text message arrives on any test phone.
evidence: Screenshot of the confirmation box showing N, and of the Outbox and History before and after.

title: Confirm a family with no usable phone number is flagged, not lost or sent to a wrong number
risk: A family never gets payment or practice messages and nobody notices, or a badly typed number sends a child's details to a stranger.
preconditions: Three test parents linked to children in the test program: one with no phone, one with a 9-digit phone (e.g. 214555010), and one with a phone typed with an extension (e.g. '214-555-0101 x12').
Make these edits in Students, and only on test parents.
steps: Go to Messaging > Compose, click By Program, choose the test program and note how many recipients are shown and which names.
Type a short message and click Send.
Open Outbox and find the cards for the three test parents.
For each card, note which buttons are offered and what number is shown.
expected: Every test parent appears in the Outbox. None is silently dropped.
The parent with no phone and the parent with a 9-digit phone show 'No usable phone number on file.' with only Skip available (no WhatsApp or Text).

The number with an extension ('214-555-0101 x12') opens WhatsApp to 214-555-0101: the extension is dropped. It never opens a different, longer number. (Fixed 2 Oct: an extension used to become a stranger's 12-digit number.)
The owner can see from the cards who could not be reached.
evidence: Screenshot of each of the three cards, and of the WhatsApp screen if the extension case opens one.

title: Compose one message to everyone in a program and check the recipient list and personalisation
risk: A message meant for one session goes to the wrong families, misses some, duplicates others, or arrives reading 'Hi {{parent_name}}'.
preconditions: A test program with at least three test children: one with two linked parents, two siblings sharing one parent, and one withdrawn (not active) child.
Write down which parents should receive the message before starting.
steps: Go to Messaging > Compose. Click By Program and select the test program (programs are listed as 'School — Program').
Compare the recipient chips and the 'N recipient(s)' count with your expected list.
From 'Use a template...' choose any template that contains {{parent_name}}, or type 'Hi {{parent_name}}, practice moves to 5pm.' using the variable buttons.
Click 'Send to N recipient(s)'.
Open Outbox and read each new card's text in full.
Repeat using By School for the test school, and note whether each parent of a child at that school appears once.
expected: Recipients are exactly the parents of active children in the program: both parents of the two-parent child, the siblings' shared parent once, and nobody for the withdrawn child.
The count on the button equals the number of cards created in the Outbox.

Each message greets the parent by their own first name. Compose fills in {{parent_name}} only; a message with any other placeholder (e.g. {{student_name}}) is refused with 'A message to a group can only fill in {{parent_name}}…' and nothing goes to the Outbox. No card ever shows a raw {{…}}.
By School lists each parent once, even if they have children in several programs at that school.
evidence: Your expected recipient list, a screenshot of the recipient chips and count, and screenshots of every resulting Outbox card.

title: Edit a message template and confirm only future messages change
risk: Editing the wording rewrites messages already prepared, or a careless edit or delete silently breaks automatic reminders and payment links.
preconditions: One pending test message in the Outbox created from a template (e.g. through Compose using 'Use a template...').
Screenshot that template's current wording on the Templates tab so it can be restored.
steps: Go to Messaging > Templates. Click Edit on the template used and change one word in Message Body only (do not change the Name). Click 'Update Template'.
Open Outbox and read the pending message created before the edit.
Create a new message to the test program using the same template and read the new card.
Put the template wording back and click 'Update Template'.

Observation only, do not complete: click Delete on any template and note whether you are asked to confirm. If it deletes immediately, restore it with Add Template using the same Name, Category and Body, and record an exception.
expected: Toast 'Template updated'. The Templates card shows the new wording.
The message already in the Outbox still has the OLD wording.
The new message uses the NEW wording.

Deleting a template you added asks 'Delete the "<name>" template?'. The templates the app sends on its own (payment_reminder, practice_reminder_day_before, practice_reminder_morning, welcome_message, session_cancelled, payment_received, autopay_invite, autopay_failed) can be reworded but not deleted: trying shows 'This message is sent automatically, so it can be reworded but not deleted.' Changing their Name has no effect.
evidence: Screenshots of the template before and after, the old and new Outbox cards, and what happens when Delete is clicked.

title: Re-run invoice generation for a month and confirm no duplicates are created
risk: Families are billed twice for the same month, and autopay could charge them twice.
preconditions: The owner has already generated the current month's invoices (check the Invoices tab for this month's entries).
Agree with the owner first: Generate Invoices bills EVERY active enrolment, not just test ones, so any real child enrolled since the last run will be billed.
Count this month's invoices on Payments > Invoices (use the Month column) and write the number down.
steps: On Payments, click Generate Invoices.
Leave the Month as the current month and click 'Generate Invoices'. Read the toast before it disappears, or record the screen.
Refresh and count this month's invoices again.
Click Generate Invoices again for the same month and repeat the count.
Use the student filter to check that two or three individual children each have exactly one invoice for this month per program.
expected: Toast says 'All N invoice(s) already exist for this month' (or, if new children joined, how many were created and how many already existed).
The invoice count does not change on the second run.
No child has two invoices for the same month and program.
evidence: Screen recording of both runs including the toasts, and the before and after counts.

title: Check a child with two parents is billed once and a child with no parent is reported
risk: A family is double-billed, or a child trains for free because nobody noticed they were never invoiced.
preconditions: In the test program: Child A linked to two test parents, and Child B with NO parent linked. Both are enrolled and active.
Same caution as INV-01: generating bills every active enrolment not yet invoiced this month.
steps: On Payments, click Generate Invoices, keep the current month and click 'Generate Invoices'. Record the screen so you catch every toast.
Refresh. Filter Invoices by Child A, then by Child B.
Note which parent Child A's invoice is billed to.
Click Generate Invoices again and check Child A still has one invoice.
expected: Child A has exactly one invoice for the month, billed to one of the two parents.
A warning toast appears: '1 enrollment(s) skipped — no parent linked to student' (the number covers all such children).
Child B has no invoice. The warning should let the owner identify WHICH child was skipped, but it gives only a count. Record whether the owner could find Child B from what the screen shows.

Invoices are always due on the 1st of the month, so an invoice created after the 1st becomes overdue as soon as the Payments page reloads. Record whether Child A's new invoice shows Overdue immediately.
evidence: Screen recording with the toasts, and screenshots of the filtered invoice lists for Child A and Child B.

title: Record a partial payment, then the balance, and check the invoice status at each step
risk: An invoice shows Paid when money is still owed, or stays owed after it has been paid, and parents are chased wrongly.
preconditions: A test invoice for a test child, status Pending or Overdue, with a known amount (e.g. $100.00) and no payments.
steps: On Payments > Invoices, click Record Payment on the test invoice. Note 'Amount Due' and 'Remaining' in the dialog.
Change Amount to less than the total (e.g. 40.00), set Method to Zelle and Reference to 'AUDIT-1'. Click Record Payment.
Check the invoice's Status and the Payment History tab.
Click Record Payment on the same invoice again. Check that 'Remaining' shows the balance (e.g. $60.00) and that the Amount box defaults to it.

Exception checks before paying the balance: try Amount 0, then -10, then an amount larger than the balance. Note what is accepted. Delete any payment that should not have been accepted (Payment History > bin icon).
Record the exact balance with Reference 'AUDIT-2'. Check the Status.
Click 'Record Payment' at the top right of Payments, enter $1, and find the test family in the list. Read what it says they owe, then close without recording.
expected: After the partial payment, the toast reads 'Payment recorded' and the invoice stays Pending (or Overdue if past due), not Paid.
Payment History shows the $40.00 Zelle payment with reference AUDIT-1 and today's date.
Remaining shows the correct balance.

Zero and negative amounts are refused ('Enter an amount greater than $0.'). An amount above the balance is refused with 'That's more than the $X still owed…'. Nothing is recorded in Payment History for any refused attempt.
After the balance is paid, the invoice shows Paid and the Record Payment and Waive buttons disappear from its row.
The family's line no longer counts the paid invoice in what they owe ('nothing owed' if that was their only one).
evidence: Screenshots of the dialog showing Remaining at each step, the invoice row after each payment, Payment History, and any invalid amounts that were accepted.

title: Edit and delete payments, and edit an invoice, and check the status follows the money
risk: Corrections to the books leave invoices marked Paid with nothing received, or marked owed after full payment.
preconditions: The fully paid test invoice from INV-03, with two payments (AUDIT-1 and AUDIT-2).
steps: On Payment History, click the pencil on AUDIT-2. Reduce the amount by $10 and click 'Save Changes'. Check the invoice status.
Edit AUDIT-2 back to the original amount. Check the status.
Delete AUDIT-2 (bin icon, confirm). Check the status.
Re-record AUDIT-2 so the invoice is Paid again.
Control check: on a different, unpaid test invoice, click the pencil (Edit Invoice), change Status to Paid without recording any payment, and click 'Save Changes'.
Control check: on a partly paid test invoice, lower the Amount until it equals what has been paid. Refresh and check the status.
expected: Reducing a payment below the total returns the invoice to Pending (or Overdue if the due date has passed), with a 'Payment updated' toast.
Restoring the amount returns it to Paid.
Deleting a payment returns it to Pending or Overdue, with a 'Payment deleted' toast, and the payment disappears from Payment History.
Marking an invoice Paid by hand has no effect: the status is worked out from payments, so it stays Pending or Overdue. Only Waived can be chosen by hand.
Lowering the invoice amount to equal what was paid makes it Paid straight away (the status is recalculated whenever an invoice is edited).
evidence: Screenshot of the invoice row status after each of the six steps.

title: Waive an invoice, and try to delete an invoice that still has payments
risk: A waived fee keeps being chased, or deleting an invoice erases money already received from the books.
preconditions: Two test invoices to waive: one with no payments and one partly paid.
Two more test invoices to delete: one with at least one payment and one with none.
Note the Pending, Overdue and Total Revenue cards before starting.
steps: Click Waive on the unpaid test invoice. Read the confirmation and click Cancel. Confirm nothing changed.
Click Waive again and confirm.
Check the row, the Waived filter, and the Pending and Overdue cards.
Waive the partly paid invoice. Check its payment still appears in Payment History and in Total Revenue.
Click 'Record Payment' at the top right, enter $1, and find each test family in the list. Read what it says they owe, then close without recording.
Click the bin icon on the invoice to delete that has a payment, and confirm 'Delete this invoice?'. Check the message, the invoice list, Payment History and Total Revenue.
Delete that invoice's payments from Payment History, then delete the invoice. Then delete the test invoice that never had payments.
expected: The confirmation reads 'Waive this invoice?'. Cancel changes nothing.
After confirming: toast 'Invoice waived', status badge 'waived', no Record Payment or Waive buttons on the row, and the invoice appears under the Waived filter.
The Pending or Overdue card drops by the invoice amount.

The partly paid invoice's payment stays recorded and counted in Total Revenue. Record whether the screen shows how much was waived versus collected. It does not record who waived the invoice or why; note this as an audit-trail gap.
Waived invoices are not counted in what a family owes, so no new payment would be put on them.
Deleting an invoice that has payments is refused with 'Delete the payments first before deleting this invoice'. The invoice and payment remain and Total Revenue is unchanged.

Once its payments are gone, the invoice deletes with 'Invoice deleted'. An invoice with no payments deletes directly. Record as an audit-trail observation that deletions leave no visible trail on screen (who, when).
evidence: Screenshots of the waive confirmation, the rows before and after, the summary cards before and after, and the delete refusal with the invoice still listed.

title: Confirm an invoice becomes overdue only after its due date, including in the evening Central time
risk: Parents are told they are late on the day payment is due, or the evening before, which damages trust and triggers wrong reminders.
preconditions: Two unpaid test invoices with no payments.
Part 2 must be done in the evening, after 7pm Central time (after 6pm Central once clocks change on 1 November), when the server's clock has already moved to tomorrow.
steps: Part 1 (daytime): click the pencil on test invoice 1. Set Due Date to TODAY's date and Status to Pending. Click 'Save Changes'.
Refresh the Payments page (opening the page is what updates overdue statuses). Note the status.
Edit test invoice 2: set Due Date to YESTERDAY and Status to Pending, save and refresh. Note the status.
Part 2 (evening, after 7pm Central): set test invoice 1's Due Date to today's date again and Status to Pending, save, and refresh the page twice. Note the status and the Overdue card count.
Next morning: refresh Payments and check test invoice 1.
expected: An invoice due today shows 'pending' in the daytime AND in the evening, and is not counted in the Overdue card.
An invoice due yesterday shows 'overdue' and is included in the Overdue (N) card.
The next morning, test invoice 1 (now due yesterday) shows 'overdue'.
Clock cross-check: write down the exact time and confirm your computer is set to Central time.
evidence: Screenshots with the computer clock visible, showing the invoice due date, status and Overdue card in the daytime, the evening and the next morning.

title: Reconcile the four summary cards to the invoice and payment lists
risk: The owner makes decisions and reports income from dashboard totals that do not agree with the underlying records.
preconditions: Payments page open, and no one else recording payments while you work.
A spreadsheet for the figures. Include at least one partly paid invoice in the data (from INV-03 or a fresh test invoice).
steps: Record the four cards: Total Revenue, Pending, Overdue (N) and Paid This Month.
Payment History tab: add up every payment Amount. Separately, add up the payments dated in the current month.
Invoices tab: click Pending and add up Amount, then click Processing and add up Amount. Click Overdue, count the rows and add up Amount. Note any of these invoices that have part-payments.
Compare: Total Revenue with all payments; Paid This Month with this month's payments; Pending with the Pending plus Processing invoices; and the Overdue amount and count with the Overdue list.
Evening check (last day of a month, after 7pm Central): record a $1 test payment, note Paid This Month and the date shown in Payment History, then delete the payment.
expected: Total Revenue equals the sum of all payments ever recorded (all time, not just this month).
Paid This Month equals payments received in the current calendar month, Central time.
Pending equals the total of the Pending and Processing invoices. Overdue equals the total of the Overdue invoices, and N equals the number of rows.
For partly paid invoices, the Pending and Overdue cards count only what is still OWED (e.g. $100 invoice with $40 paid adds $60). Reconcile the cards to the sum of balances, not invoice amounts.
Evening check: a payment recorded on the last evening of a month (Central time) counts in that month's 'Paid This Month'.
evidence: The reconciliation spreadsheet with every figure, plus screenshots of the cards and each filtered list.

title: Generate weekly sessions and confirm no week is missing or duplicated
risk: A practice is missing from the schedule (no reminders, no register) or doubled (double reminders, confusing records).
preconditions: Under Schedule > Manage Templates, the test program has a weekly template (e.g. Tuesday 4:00 PM – 5:00 PM). Ideally, add a second test template on a weekday EARLIER in the week than today, and a third on today's weekday.
The test program has no end date within the next 4 weeks.
Generate Sessions creates the next 4 weeks for EVERY template, real ones included. This is normally harmless because existing sessions are skipped.
steps: Click Manage Templates and note each test template's day and time.
Close it and click Generate Sessions. Note the toast.
Refresh the page (the grid may not update by itself). Use the arrows and the Today button to step through the next 4 weeks.
For each test template, list the dates on which a session appears.
Click Generate Sessions again, refresh and re-check.
expected: Toast reads 'N session(s) generated'.

Each template has exactly one session in each of the next 4 weeks, on the correct weekday and time, starting today if today is that weekday. There are no gaps and no two sessions on the same date and time.
No sessions are created in the past or after the program's end date.
The second run reports '0 session(s) generated' and nothing is duplicated.
If the grid did not show the new sessions until a refresh, note it as a usability issue. If a run with no templates reports '0 session(s) generated' instead of an error, note that too.
evidence: Screenshots of Manage Templates, the toasts, and each of the 4 weeks in the grid.

title: Check sessions show on the right day in the week grid and Session Details, in the evening too
risk: Coaches and the owner turn up on the wrong day, or attendance is taken against the wrong date.
preconditions: Test sessions generated (SCH-01) on a known weekday, e.g. Tuesday.
Computer set to Central time. Part 2 must be done after 7pm Central (after 6pm Central from 1 November).
steps: Daytime: open Schedule. Note which day column the test Tuesday session appears under, and which column is highlighted as today.
Click the session. In Session Details, note the date line, program name and school name.
Evening (after 7pm Central): repeat both steps without changing anything else.
Compare all four observations with the template's day in Manage Templates.
expected: The session appears under Tue at all hours, and the today highlight is on today's real date.
Session Details shows the same date (e.g. 'Tuesday, October 6'), plus the program and school names.

Record a separate exception for each of these if it happens: in the evening, sessions appear one column off; at any time, Session Details shows the day before the grid's day; the program or school name is blank.
evidence: Screenshots of the grid and Session Details, daytime and evening, with the computer clock visible.

title: Cancel a session and confirm it stays cancelled and cannot be used
risk: Parents get a reminder for a cancelled practice, or a cancelled session quietly reappears or is used to record attendance.
preconditions: A future test session in the grid, with status scheduled.
steps: Click the session, then Cancel Session. Leave the reason box ('Reason (optional)') empty and click Confirm Cancel. Note the message.
Type a reason (e.g. 'Audit test – gym closed') and click Confirm Cancel.
Check the grid, then reopen the session.
Click Generate Sessions and refresh. Check the date again.
If the cancelled session is tomorrow: the next morning, check Messaging > Outbox for any practice reminder for it.
expected: With no reason, the cancellation is refused ('The session wasn't cancelled' with 'Cancellation reason is required.'). The box is labelled optional, so record this as a labelling mismatch.
With a reason: toast 'Session cancelled', and the session shows faded and struck through, with a Cancelled badge.
When reopened, it shows status 'cancelled' and no Save Attendance or Coach link buttons.
Generating again does not recreate it.
No practice reminder is prepared for a cancelled session. Record that the app does not tell parents about the cancellation itself; the owner must message them.
evidence: Screenshots of the error, the cancelled tile, the reopened dialog, and the Outbox the next morning.

title: Take attendance from the dashboard and confirm it is saved correctly
risk: The register is wrong or lost, so the business cannot show who attended (safeguarding and billing disputes).
preconditions: A scheduled test session for a test program with at least four active test children and one withdrawn test child.
steps: Click the session. Check the list of children against the active enrolment.
Click children to cycle their status: leave one present, and set one absent, one late and one excused.
Check the 'x/y' counter, then click Save Attendance.
Close and reopen the session. Check each child's status.
Click Mark Complete. Reopen the session.
expected: Only active children are listed. The withdrawn child is not.
Clicking cycles present > absent > late > excused > present, and the counter counts present and late.
Toast 'Attendance saved'. On reopening, every status is as you set it.

After Mark Complete the badge shows 'completed'. Note whether the saved register can still be viewed. If it is hidden once the session is complete, record that attendance evidence for completed sessions cannot be reviewed on screen.
evidence: Screenshots before saving, after reopening, and after Mark Complete.

title: Send a coach the passcode link and take the register on a phone
risk: Coaches cannot take the register at the gym, so attendance is not recorded.
preconditions: A scheduled test session today or soon, with active test children. One test child has a medical note.
A phone that is NOT logged in to the app (use a private browsing window).
steps: On the computer, open the session and click Coach link. Note the link, the 6-digit passcode and the validity text. Click 'Copy link and passcode' and send it to the phone by WhatsApp.
Close and reopen the session dialog. Note whether the passcode can be seen again.
On the phone, open the link. Check the screen before entering anything.
Enter the passcode and tap Open register.
Tap names to set one child Away and one Late, then tap Save register.
On the computer, reopen the session and check the statuses.
expected: A box 'Send this to the coach' shows a link ending /s/..., a 6-digit passcode, and 'Valid for 12 hours. The passcode isn't shown again — copy it now.' The copied text includes the link and the passcode.
After reopening, the passcode is not shown again.
On the phone, before the passcode is entered, the page shows only 'Take the register' and a passcode box, with no child names. Open register stays disabled until 6 digits are entered.
After unlocking, the page shows the program, school, date and time, 'N of M here', the active children, their medical notes, and Here/Away/Late/Excused buttons.
Save register changes to 'Saved ✓', and the dashboard shows the same statuses.
evidence: Screenshots of the coach link box, the phone before and after unlocking, the saved state, and the matching dashboard view.

title: Lock a coach link with wrong passcodes, and confirm replaced, expired and cancelled-session links are refused
risk: Anyone who has or guesses a link could see children's names and medical notes, and old links keep working after they should not.
preconditions: A fresh coach link and passcode for a test session (Coach link button), opened on a phone in a private window.
A timer.
For the replaced-link check: a second Coach link issued for the same session. There is no separate Revoke button; issuing a new link is the only way to switch off the old one.
For the expiry check: a link issued at least 12 hours before testing.
steps: Enter a wrong 6-digit passcode and tap Open register. Note the message.
Repeat with different wrong passcodes until you have made 5 wrong attempts.
Now enter the CORRECT passcode. Note the message and the time.
Try the correct passcode again after 5 minutes, and again after 16 minutes.
Optional: change one character of the link and enter the correct passcode.

Issue link A for a test session and confirm it unlocks. Then close and reopen the session and click Coach link again to issue link B. On the phone, open link A with passcode A, then link B with passcode B.
Try a link issued more than 12 hours ago with its correct passcode.
Issue a link for another test session, cancel that session (with a reason), then open the link with its passcode.
expected: Each wrong attempt shows 'That link or passcode is not right.' and no child data.
After 5 wrong attempts, even the correct passcode is refused with 'Too many wrong passcodes. Try again in a few minutes, or ask for a new link.'
The link is still locked after 5 minutes and works again after about 15 minutes.
A tampered link gives the same 'not right' message, which reveals nothing about whether the link exists.
Link A is refused with 'This link has been turned off. Ask for a new one.' Link B works.
The 12-hour-old link is refused with 'This link has expired. Ask for a new one.'

A link for a cancelled session should be refused. If it still opens and allows saving, record an exception. Also record as an observation that the owner cannot switch off a link without issuing a new one.
evidence: Screen recording of all passcode attempts with a clock visible. Screenshots of the lock message, the later successful unlock with times, and each refusal message with the time the link was issued and the time it was tested.

title: Check the coach register shows only what a coach needs (data minimisation)
risk: A coach, or anyone a link is forwarded to, sees parents' phone numbers, addresses, fees or children from other sessions.
preconditions: A test session with test children whose records include parent names, phone numbers, emails, fees owed and medical notes.
A valid coach link and passcode, opened on a phone in a private window.
steps: Unlock the register on the phone.
Read the whole page, scrolling to the bottom, and list every piece of information shown.
Tap each child's name and check that nothing extra appears.
Look for any link or button that leads elsewhere in the app.
